title: Wrapping Up a Story: végül, eredmény, lezár

sections.title: Closing the sequence, not just adding one more event
sections.content: You already know végül ("finally, in the end") for the last event in a chain. Two more words let you step back from the events themselves and name what they added up to: eredmény ("result, outcome") and lezár ("to close, to conclude") — a transitive verb, so it needs a definite or indefinite object just like any other.

sections.title: Closing a story
rows: In the end, we got home.
Az eredmény az volt, hogy mindenki elkésett.
The result was that everyone was late.
Egy közös vacsorával zártuk le a napot.
We closed the day with a shared dinner.

items.spanish: Sokáig kerestük az utat, végül egy helyi asszony eligazított minket.
items.english: We looked for the way for a long time; in the end, a local woman set us straight.

items.spanish: Az eredmény az lett, hogy három órát késtünk.
items.english: The result was that we ended up three hours late.

items.spanish: Egy hosszú beszélgetéssel zártuk le a vitát.
items.english: We closed the argument with a long conversation.

sections.content: Az eredmény az volt/lett, hogy... ("the result was that...") is a ready-made frame for stepping outside the story to comment on it — useful right before the very end, once the events themselves are already told.
